Drain wallet, Osmosis — same key as the Cosmos Hub drain.
Drain wallet, Injective — holds the stolen INJ, USDT and USDC.
Reported on X by Katie V Holmes Nov 7 2026 (same key as the Cosmos address); chains asked to freeze.
Batch fee payer — funded by exactly 3 transfers totaling 228.61 ATOM; made 2,520 self-sends of 1 uatom, one per tokenize batch (Nov 7 09:57–15:33 UTC).
Control wallet — rehearsed every step of the attack before going live (seeded test accounts, cross-chain IBC tests, LSM rehearsal). Its key spans 8 chains.
Test wallet, Osmosis — the operator’s cross-chain rehearsal hub. Its first-ever Osmosis drain send (Nov 6 21:08:30 UTC) was a test.
Test wallet, Cosmos Hub — operator-seeded (0.03 ATOM from the control wallet), then forwarded 26,253 uatom to the drain wallet Nov 6 21:57:39 UTC. Not a victim.
Test wallet, Cosmos Hub — operator-seeded, then forwarded 26,253 uatom to the drain wallet Nov 6 21:57:39 UTC. Not a victim.
Funding source — identity UNVERIFIED (exchange label unconfirmed). Attack-linked transfers: 8.46 ATOM to the control wallet, 45.70 + 109.62 ATOM to the fee payer (163.78 ATOM total).
Funding source — identity UNVERIFIED (exchange label unconfirmed). In 225,297.75 ATOM, out 234,474.75 ATOM; its only attack-linked transfer is 73.29 ATOM to the fee payer.
Test wallet, Babylon — same wtdg key as the control wallet; sent the BBN seed (9,773,023 ubbn) to the Babylon drain wallet Nov 7 02:38:08 UTC.

Attacker's own Celestia address (same key as the Osmosis swapper osmo1w05l… — payload 73e9fdbe…). Received 33,096.36 TIA via IBC from Osmosis Nov 2 00:20:58 UTC (tx 6AB14050…, height 73820352). Final destination of the stolen AKT's phase-2 proceeds — Sith Lord case (Nov 1 theft, separate from the Keplr drain). Now holds only ~8.28 TIA (seq 16); most has moved on.

incident.affected: Keplr wallets created with Google/Apple login. Community analysis: most victims imported their seed phrases into Keplr; wallets created in the browser extension and backed up as a file were most likely hit. Evmos was also drained Nov 6.
incident.attacker: UNKNOWN — no attacker has been publicly named and no verified attacker wallet addresses have been published yet. Whoever controls the stolen funds has not cashed out anything so far.
incident.cause: Web3Auth infrastructure vulnerability leading to a private key breach (Keplr, Nov 7). Community on-chain analysis (Nov 7): Web3Auth published MPC key shares and seed phrases in public GitHub repos (recorded May 22, 2025); the attacker collected them and waited. Affected wallets were mostly created in 2024 or earlier.
incident.safe: Seed-phrase and hardware wallets are NOT affected (confirmed again by Keplr Nov 7). If you used Google/Apple login: do not send new funds to that account; move any remaining liquid assets to a recovery-phrase or hardware-wallet account. Do not export the social-login account’s keys into another wallet. Keplr + Web3Auth are building a checker for whether your account is affected.

timeline.event: Web3Auth pauses its embedded-wallet service after a security issue affecting third parties.
Keplr flags unauthorized transactions on some Google/Apple-login accounts.
Keplr posts its notice: social (Google/Apple) login paused; users told not to add funds or re-import those accounts.
Keplr co-founder Josh Lee: incident originated at Web3Auth; ~20% of social-login accounts affected, only a fraction drained; remaining accounts may be recoverable.
No confirmed loss total or drained-wallet count has been published by Keplr or Web3Auth. Earlier circulating figures were wrong and are not used here.

Attacker wallet addresses reported on X by Katie V Holmes (@lady_in_c...): cosmos1atuap9kfnt6y8ykvn3437e7j3z8qffh3qtnmwu, osmo1atuap9kfnt6y8ykvn3437e7j3z8qffh3gsqtcw, inj1lqmdmuczn5rxn5jkc34wwrqdeh70etpf5wvt7g, bbn1atuap9kfnt6y8ykvn3437e7j3z8qffh3h4z239. Chains asked to freeze them. All four are now watched live on this tracker.
Web3Auth disclosed the vulnerability to its customers (“revoke this key”). The alert was closed as “already solved”.
First known drain — a single Cosmos address empties 397 wallets.
Evmos, the Cosmos EVM chain, was drained too.
First drain attack begins on Osmosis; the attack takes off on Cosmos Hub.
First Cosmos Hub drain confirmed — $18,000 in STRD and ATOM.
Attacker drained $21k and $39k in 90 minutes.
Community on-chain analysis publishes totals: $4.56M, 41,500+ wallets, 3 chains, $0 cashed out.
First drain send observed on-chain: a victim sends 26,253 uatom to the Cosmos drain wallet. (On-chain block scan)
Biggest wave: 13,181 victim sends, 219,785 ATOM swept in under 2 hours. (On-chain block scan)

On-chain scan confirms 42,363 victim sends from 24,660 distinct senders into the Cosmos drain wallet; drain active at that time (later scans confirm it ended 15:33:49 UTC); $0 moved out of any of the 4 wallets. Cosmos drain wallet holds 532,933 ATOM.
LSM finding: 99.7% of the LSM tokens in the drain wallet were created during the incident (record IDs 120,000+) — victims’ staked ATOM tokenised in bulk instead of waiting 21 days to unbond.
Final drain burst: 1 BBN + 9 OSMO + 7 INJ sends in the same minute on three chains. Last activity on Osmosis, Injective and Babylon.
Last Cosmos Hub activity (LSM batch). Full block scans confirm the drain is OVER on all four chains; $0 has moved out of any drain wallet. (On-chain block scan, part 2)

Verified totals: Osmosis 29,280 sends / 29,248 senders / 1,788,487.64 OSMO; Injective 7,606 successful sends / 7,603 senders / 67,987.05 INJ (404 failed, out of gas); Babylon 749 sends / 748 senders / 1,407,799.79 BBN. No IBC hops between drain wallets. (On-chain block scan, part 2)

Supporting wallets traced: fee payer funded by 3 transfers totaling 228.61 ATOM with 2,520 batch self-sends; control wallet rehearsed every step; the wtdg key spans 8 chains (Cosmos, Osmosis, Babylon, Noble, dYdX, Axelar, Saga, Agoric). Funding-source identities remain unverified. (On-chain block scan, part 2)

Keplr: “What this means for Keplr users” — seed/hardware wallets NOT affected (confirmed again). Web3Auth infrastructure vulnerability led to a private key breach. Keplr + Web3Auth are actively securing/protecting assets; some Google/Apple accounts may show a reduced or empty balance as a result of that mitigation, not theft. Advice: do not send new funds; move remaining liquid assets to a seed/hardware account. A checker for whether your account is affected is being built. Only trust @keplrwallet / @Web3Auth; ignore “recovery” DMs.

Web3Auth: whitehat recovery is moving funds out of vulnerable (not yet drained) wallets using the same path as the attacker — some of these transfers look like attacker activity but are recovery, and the funds are safe. Web3Auth will publish a verified list of recovery addresses; until then, trust only addresses from official Web3Auth/Keplr channels — any other recovery address may be phishing.
Keplr: recovery operations may explain some empty social-login balances. Web3Auth plans a verified list so users can identify recovery transfers. (The Defiant)

Community report — Sith Lord ($ATOM OG Community Chat): wallet osmo10p7dg5nh8kwjhfucq0uxjppg6wkevzmg67c4hx reported as holding stolen funds; he lost 40,000+ AKT, which the attacker moved to another AKT address then swapped for OSMO ~1,000 AKT at a time. On-chain check: the wallet holds 3,853,217.84 OSMO, seq 13007 (old active account, not a seq-0 drain wallet); its only funder is osmo13pet0rwjjzgz7f3058xklc2y05eg5cjneaad94, which still holds 579.19 AKT; it received 2,499,999.87 OSMO during the drain (Nov 7 ~09:30 UTC) and never sent to the main Osmosis drain wallet. Reported case, under investigation — new tab added to the tracker.

Sith Lord posted his AKT account (akash1vk6mqt3jaxu4ys9a2849qu2u0k0kt8kuajg5dv) — his 40,066.86 AKT theft (Nov 1, 21:19-21:20 UTC) is traced on-chain: akash1vk6m… → akash1w05lm0ng2y6wfthhwtqsmuc7xx83j7r49406f4 (txs 5A82C4FC73BE688B… / 5DCDA1DCF643A311…) → IBC to Osmosis (tx CEA57DBAE1A47C21…, channel-9 → channel-1, packet 485820) → osmo1w05lm0ng2y6wfthhwtqsmuc7xx83j7r4q43dxa, which swapped the AKT away. The theft predates the Keplr hack by 5 days — likely a separate theft. CORRECTION (hunt part 3): the final hop is now PROVEN — 9 lockstep tx pairs (each funder→case send exactly 0.13 OSMO less than the matching w05→funder send); the funder sent 7,890,851.15 OSMO to the case wallet in 51 transfers. Full AKT reconciliation: 12,888 AKT → 159,744 OSMO + 27,178.85 AKT → 33,096.36 TIA, IBC'd to the attacker's Celestia address celestia1w05lm0ng2y6wfthhwtqsmuc7xx83j7r4eynd2z (tx 6AB14050…). The 7xpfv 'marker key' is the chains' fee_collector module account (gas fees), NOT an operator tag. His AKT account now holds 0.003 AKT.

Hunt part 3 complete — Sith Lord theft fully traced and proven on-chain. 13th wallet now tracked: the attacker's Celestia address celestia1w05lm0ng2y6wfthhwtqsmuc7xx83j7r4eynd2z (same key as the Osmosis swapper; received the 33,096.36 TIA Nov 2; now holds only ~8.28 TIA — most moved on, onward destination not yet traced). Note: the hunt report first labeled the IBC'd funds 'stablecoins'; the denom trace + hash check prove ibc/D79E… is TIA. Case wallet unchanged at 3,853,217.84 OSMO, seq 13007 (re-verified 14:14 EST); funder unchanged at 4,615.43 OSMO + 579.19 AKT. Overlap found: two wallets that funded the funder were later swept by the Keplr drain (osmo1n3yyv… / osmo1xadzkk…) — the clusters share victims, but the thefts are separate.

Sith Lord case wallet moved again: sequence 13007 → 13009 (2 sends) and balance fell ~58,319 OSMO (3,853,217.84 → 3,794,898.98 OSMO) since the 14:14 EST re-verification — continued distribution from the attacker-controlled consolidation wallet. The second cluster wallet osmo1ctpu5… is unchanged at 3,879,800.09 OSMO. All 4 drain wallets still sequence 0 — $0 out.

Hunt part 4 complete — the origin chain, from Wandering Cosmonaut's idea. The drain started Nov 6 20:52:37 UTC (10 × 13,242 uatom rehearsal batch), 65 minutes earlier than first reported. The operator funding chain runs back to Aug 17, 2026 — then the public nodes run out (pruned to Aug 17 13:47 UTC); no single origin wallet exists in the observable trail. New 'Where It Started' tab with the full A–Z chain.

Hunt part 5 complete — Sith Lord's second wallet traced and proven: osmo1ctpu5… holds 3,879,800 OSMO, active since Aug 11, ~39.9M OSMO sent to 138 wallets. Relay osmo180qdt2… carried 222,611 OSMO from the case wallet to it in 4 lockstep forwards (Nov 5–7); it fed the funder 1,228,994 OSMO in Aug–Oct, before the theft — the senior hub of the same operation. Different key, never sent to the Keplr drain wallets. New lead: osmo1re9zkt… sent it 2,222,173.88 OSMO. Added to the Sith Lord tab.

Sith Lord second cluster wallet osmo1ctpu5… moved again: sequence 3752 → 3753 (1 send), balance fell ~30,977 OSMO (3,879,800.09 → 3,848,823.55 OSMO) since the 15:36 EST check — continued distribution. STRD balance unchanged at 1,809,440.59. Destination of the send not yet identified (Osmosis tx index unavailable). Case wallet unchanged at 3,794,898.98 OSMO, seq 13009. All 4 drain wallets still sequence 0 — $0 out.

Sith Lord freeze ask — outcome from Osmosis (Jason Banfield): a freeze is only possible with a chain upgrade, and any freeze/seize would be done in bulk (all accounts together, not individual accounts); he shared the case with the team and validators. The user sent Jason the full flag package (case wallet, funder, ctpu + the 3 theft tx hashes + tracker link). Jason: Osmosis can't flag on exchanges, and exchanges usually only act after a police/cybercrime report is filed — so the police report is now the key step that unlocks exchange action.

Jason Banfield added: the victim himself has to ask the exchanges (it's his wallet) — Osmosis can't do that for him. He also asked internally if Osmosis has any way to flag, and said if anybody does it would be Keplr wallet, as they are core to everything Cosmos. So the exchange-flag route runs through Sith Lord himself, plus Keplr.

Jason Banfield: he has done what he can — he requested input from the validators and the team and doesn't want to overstep; he seems to be the only one active on Osmosis Slack all day. Josh from Keplr is active at 4am his time. The Osmosis route is now exhausted; the live contacts are Sith Lord himself (exchanges + police report) and Keplr.

totals.takenNote: Per-chain (community on-chain analysis, Nov 7, at ATOM $1.39 / INJ $8.24): Cosmos Hub ~$2.93M (466,000 ATOM + 1.65M ATOM tokenised stake); Osmosis ~$1.01M (1,239 different tokens); Injective ~$616K. Verified on-chain (part-2 scan): Osmosis 1,788,487.64 OSMO, Injective 67,987.05 INJ, Babylon 1,407,799.79 BBN. Injective USDT/USDC totals (53,466 USDT / 2,031 USDC) were NOT independently verified. LP shares and small tokens not counted, so the real total is higher.
totals.walletsNote: Per-chain: Cosmos Hub 18,600+; Osmosis 29,100+; Injective 7,596. Per-chain counts sum higher than 41,500+ because one seed phrase appears on multiple chains. On-chain scans observed 62,259 distinct senders across the 4 chains (Cosmos 24,660 + Osmosis 29,248 + Injective 7,603 + Babylon 748), but the same seed appears on multiple chains so the true victim count is lower.
totals.cashedOutNote: Nothing has left any of the 4 drain wallets — all have sequence 0 (never signed a transaction), confirmed by full block scans of all four chains Nov 7 ~17:00 UTC. The drain is OVER: last activity Nov 7 10:34 UTC on Osmosis, Injective and Babylon, and 15:33:49 UTC on Cosmos Hub. Circle can freeze ~$188K of Noble USDC in the Osmosis drain wallet.
